mechanism: One32-dimension CTA with6*M warps. Each speculative row owns six independent head warps and one FP32 accumulator per lane. Shared four-buffer64-position V ring is produced once for all rows; row/head probability rings remain distinct. Fixed32 CTAs cover all KV heads and256 dimensions. M2/3/4 block sizes384/576/768, no scan.
distinction: Closed PV row-compose used192 threads and M serial accumulators per lane. This uses independent row warps to preserve consumer concurrency while sharing V. Retained PV usesM separate CTAs and64 dimensions/two accumulators per lane. This is one coupled producer/consumer architecture, not a repair or parameter scan of either old arrangement.
equivalence: For each(row,head,dimension), accumulator starts+0 and consumes original ascending-position fma.rn.f32(P,V,acc) through actual first_sequence+row, then original BF16 RNE once. Shared V may include later rows but earlier consumers never use them. All threads advance rings/barriers through the longest sequence; each warp masks only arithmetic and probability valid bytes to its own causal length. QK, full FP32 softmax probabilities, projections, state and draft unchanged.

traffic_trade: At fixed sequence, V demand is shared across M rows but probability demand doubles relative to64-dimension incumbent. Separate consumer warps remove per-thread M accumulator serialization; increased block size can reduce scheduling flexibility. These are source-level demands, not measuredDRAM or occupancy claims.
